sector_alerts.title: Israel/Palestine: West Bank settler attack near Nablus kills four Palestinians and two Israelis (Jul 24)
sector_alerts.summary: Armed settlers stormed homes and farmland at al-Tal village near Nablus on Jul 24; the confrontation escalated into gunfire that killed four Palestinians and two Israelis. Israeli forces launched a 'major counterterrorism operation,' raiding roughly 70 homes and arresting nearly 50 Palestinians in the village, while settler reprisal attacks spread to nearby communities.

sector_alerts.title: Iran: 1,500 death-row prisoners on hunger strike at Ghezel Hesar Prison since Jul 13 to protest executions
sector_alerts.summary: 1,500 death-row prisoners in Unit 2 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj have been on hunger strike and sit-in since Jul 13, triggered by the transfer of six cellmates to solitary confinement for execution. Some prisoners have begun a dry hunger strike and sewn their lips shut; several are reported in critical medical condition. The protest continues alongside the ongoing US-Iran regional war.

sector_alerts.title: DR Congo: ADF attacks kill 20+ in Beni territory (Jul 12-23); Kinshasa braces for term-extension-law protests
sector_alerts.summary: A wave of at least three ADF attacks in Beni territory, North Kivu between Jul 12 and 23 killed more than 20 people, including a church elder and worship leader; the most recent, on Jul 23, killed at least 16. Separately, demonstrations against a proposed law that could extend President Tshisekedi's term were planned in Kinshasa for Jul 22, prompting hardened international travel advisories.

sector_alerts.title: AI industry accountability: Microsoft and Meta face AI-driven layoff lawsuits; Clearview AI settlement vacated; Figure AI whistleblower suit over robot safety
sector_alerts.summary: Microsoft was sued (reported Jul 17) over ~9,000 layoffs amid AI-driven restructuring; 26 Meta employees sued (filed, reported Jul 14) alleging AI-assisted layoff selection disproportionately targeted staff on medical/parental leave. The Seventh Circuit vacated Clearview AI's biometric-privacy settlement approval on Jul 13, reopening the case. Separately, Figure AI's former head of product safety sued after alleging he was fired for raising concerns that the company's humanoid robots generate force sufficient to fracture an adult skull.

sector_alerts.title: US ICE enforcement: Houston fatal shooting (Jul 13), Las Vegas deadly-force pattern, Chicago and Sacramento policy clashes
sector_alerts.summary: ICE fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston on Jul 13 -- one of at least nine deaths connected to ICE enforcement operations through Jul 15 -- prompting street protests; Houston's City Council separately passed an ordinance limiting HPD-ICE cooperation. Las Vegas Sun investigative reporting (Jul 18) documented a pattern of deadly ICE force nationally. Chicago's City Council scrutinized Mayor Johnson's ICE-restriction plan (Jul 15) amid intensified enforcement, and DHS publicly pressured Sacramento-area sanctuary officials (Jul 24) over a detainer request.

sector_alerts.title: Higher education: Yale joins Harvard funding-freeze amicus brief (Jul 23); federal OCR opens med-school admissions probe (Jul 22)
sector_alerts.summary: Yale and other universities joined an amicus brief on Jul 23 supporting Harvard's lawsuit challenging the federal government's freeze of research grants and contracts. Separately, the Education Department's Office for Civil Rights opened investigations on Jul 22 into five medical schools over alleged racial discrimination in admissions, continuing the year's broader pattern of federal funding, DEI and antisemitism-related pressure on universities.

sector_alerts.title: Nicaragua, Honduras, Pakistan-administered Kashmir: continued state repression and unrest
sector_alerts.summary: UN rights chief Volker Turk condemned Ortega's Jul 22 threats to cancel Nicaragua's elections amid 46 arbitrary political detentions. In Honduras, a Jul 15 hearing reclassified a Garifuna community's ancestral-land eviction dispute as organized crime. In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, the UN called (Jul 17) for an independent probe into unrest that has killed at least 31 people ahead of upcoming regional elections.
